- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 1-2 day lag correction.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon show persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply downward adjustment of 1-3% if sentiment is ambiguous.
- If recent history shows strong downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a 2-5% upward bias to counteract underestimation.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3-5 days, model lags in recognizing the reversal; adjust forecast 1-2 days ahead of true turn.
